newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq's Aziz leaves for China.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Aziz leaves for China.

text.p: Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz has left for China, the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) said on Saturday.
"Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz has left Baghdad heading a delegation to Beijing on a several-day visit to China," the agency said.
Although INA did not say what the aim of the visit was, Aziz is expected to lobby for an immediate lift of the United Nations sanctions imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

The curbs include a ban on Baghdad's oil exports that will not be lifted until the U.N. Special Commission -- the body in charge of disarming Iraq -- testifies that Baghdad has no more weapons of mass destruction.
The U.N., however, has allowed Iraq since December to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy urgent needs for the Iraqis.
China, along with Russia and France, want to see an immediate lift of embargoes on Iraqi oil exports in order to revive their once lurcative trade with Baghdad.
Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said last month that his country was close to sign an oil agreement with China to develop the billion barrel Ahdab field.
